clue.text: His British agent could hang out with French

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words alongside are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's British spy might go around with a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges COULD, HANG and FRENCH together; 'with' only joins. 'His' is God, so the definition reads as God's agent in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The established national church serves as God's representative body in Britain, a whimsical reading of the national church.

clue.text: Where striker stands defiant, not easily ruffled

parts.note: in cricket the batsman on strike stands at the crease
resistant means defiant, opposing

explanation.surface: A striking worker on the picket line refuses to be shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line in cricket where the batsman stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that resists creasing stays smooth, so it is hard to ruffle or rumple.

clue.text: Happy note added to text in style of Swedish centre

parts.note: feeling up means feeling happy
PS, postscript, is a note added after a letter's text
a la, from French, means in the style of

explanation.surface: A cheerful note is appended in the manner of a Swedish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a university city in Sweden, its fourth largest.

clue.text: Working for myself in Costa Rica, I'd toe 1 across's line

indicators.note: in puts the working-for-myself pieces inside the country's code

parts.note: CR is the international code for Costa Rica
on means working, functioning
me stands for myself

explanation.surface: Self-employed in Costa Rica, I'd follow the national church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to 1 across: one who conforms to the established English church.
explanation.definitionFit: A conformer follows the rules, historically one who adhered to the established Church.

clue.text: Acid from cool EU ministers

indicators.note: from shows the letters come out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Bitter words come from calm European ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleum is fuming sulphuric acid, a solution of sulphur trioxide in sulphuric acid.

clue.text: Death keeping sick cleric confined on every side

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so death wraps around the other piece

parts.note: end is death

indicators.note: sick means unwell or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Death holds an ill priest who is hemmed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges CLERIC to CIRCLE, which END holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Encircled means surrounded, ringed round on all sides.

clue.text: Make do with pass

definitions.meaning: to manage with what one has
to get past or to scrape through

explanation.definitionFit: To get by is to manage or cope, and also to slip past something.

clue.text: Song includes rotter in rustic paradise

indicators.note: includes means the song contains the next piece

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A tune features a villain in a pastoral idyll.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised pastoral land of classical poetry, a rural utopia.

clue.text: Duke with Hamlet among misused? You cannot be serious

indicators.note: misused means used wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke and Hamlet badly treated among others: you're joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges DUKE, HAMLET and AMONG together; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom expressing disbelief, the same as saying you must be joking.

clue.text: Outgoing submarine docks in Devon water

indicators.note: in places the submarine docks within the Devon river

parts.note: the Exe is a river flowing through Devon
submarines are berthed in protected docks called pens

explanation.surface: A submarine leaves its pens and heads out into a Devon river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, used as a noun, is a cost or outlay of money.

clue.text: Guys note an image useful in medicine

parts.note: cats is slang for guys or blokes, as in cool cats
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Some men write down a picture that a doctor might find handy.
explanation.definitionFit: A computerised scan produces cross-sectional pictures of the body for diagnosis.

clue.text: Namibian guerillas trade nothing

parts.note: to trade is to swap one thing for another
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A guerrilla group in Namibia exchanges nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The South West Africa People's Organisation fought an armed struggle for Namibian independence.

clue.text: Great suffering on semi-modern line, street car going into reverse

indicators.note: going into reverse turns the whole string of pieces backwards
semi means half, so the first half of the word modern is taken

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a line
a tram is a car running on street rails

explanation.surface: A tram on a fairly modern line starts going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into reverse' turns the whole run MOD + RY + TRAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Martyrdom is extreme suffering, originally death endured for one's faith.

clue.text: Rocks broken on the way to Mardale resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so these letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Stones lie smashed along the road to Mardale, a Lake District holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, but read as re-sort it rearranges TO MARDALE. Mardale is a valley in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Road metal is broken stone used to make or repair road surfaces.

clue.text: Let prices fluctuate in sweet liqueur

indicators.note: fluctuate means vary and shift, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Allow the cost of a drink to go up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is a sweet orange-flavoured liqueur, as used in cocktails.

clue.text: Singer Chris is also known as Dicky

indicators.note: dicky means faulty or unsound, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer called Chris goes by the nickname Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a nickname but means shaky, rearranging AKA to AAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Isaak is an American singer, known for the song Wicked Game.

clue.text: Suddenly enter, seizing bombardier with good morals

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: to irrupt is to burst in suddenly
a bombardier is an artillery non-commissioned officer, an NCO

explanation.surface: Burst in, grabbing a gunner of virtuous character.
explanation.walkthrough: A bombardier is a junior NCO rank in the British artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrupt means morally upright and not open to bribery.

clue.text: Very fine evening meal down by a piano

indicators.note: down by means short of, so the meal loses a letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A lovely dinner is had beside a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down by' is read as reduced by: SUPPER loses one of its Ps.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is a casual word for excellent or very fine.

clue.text: Quip about educated woman with strict morals

indicators.note: about means around, so the quip surrounds the woman

parts.note: a pun is a witty quip
Rita is the heroine of the play Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A joke concerning a learned lady with a strict code.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a British play and film by Willy Russell.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritan as an adjective describes rigidly strict moral or religious standards.

clue.text: Nice do ruined by drink and unseemly behaviour

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the words before it are scrambled

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A nice party was spoiled by booze and bad conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum means lack of propriety, behaviour that breaks good manners.

clue.text: I arrive knackered in holiday region

indicators.note: knackered means broken or worn out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: I turn up exhausted at a holiday coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the Mediterranean coast of France and Italy, a resort area.

clue.text: Empty wood where entertainment's barely offered

parts.note: to strip a room is to empty it
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Clear out a forest where little show is put on.
explanation.walkthrough: A wood is a golf club with a large head, used for long shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where performers undress, so the show is barely clothed: a pun on barely.

clue.text: Religionist comes with Prince of Troy, last pair to turn up

indicators.note: the final two letters of the Trojan prince's name are flipped upwards, read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: Paris was a prince of Troy who carried off Helen

explanation.surface: A believer arrives with a Trojan prince, the final two appearing late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last pair to turn up' flips only the final two letters, IS becoming SI, as a down entry is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism, especially in India.

clue.text: Namibia's leader seen in club acceptable to African people

indicators.note: seen in places the letter inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club

indicators.note: leader means the first letter

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, acceptable

explanation.surface: Namibia's leader appears in a club that welcomes Africans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large family of peoples of central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Tangle with composer

explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to entangle, and Ravel is the French composer of Boléro.

clue.text: Star workers are retained

indicators.note: retained shows the workers holding the next word inside them

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Employees are being kept on, a star turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a red supergiant, the brightest star in Scorpius.

clue.text: Art movement new to Poussin

definitions.meaning: Art ..., the decorative style of around 1900
Poussin was a French painter, and the French word for new is used

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is the second word of the style's name, Art Nouveau.
explanation.definitionFit: The French adjective meaning new, as Poussin would say it, also names the Art Nouveau style.

clue.text: Was it sworn at Versailles in a tie-break situation?

definitions.text: Was it sworn at Versailles in a tie-break situation?

parts.words: Was it sworn at Versailles in a tie-break situation?
parts.note: a revolutionary pledge of 1789 made in a royal tennis hall, with a nod to a tie-break being played on court

explanation.walkthrough: In June 1789 the French Third Estate swore not to disband until France had a constitution, meeting in a real tennis hall at Versailles.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1789 pledge by French deputies was sworn in a tennis hall, hence a court where tie-breaks happen.
